action.mutates: creates the empty directory /var/tmp/p8test-fs-health (the check itself only reads)
creates /var/tmp/p8test-fs-health with five 4 KB files of random data (20 KB, above the 8 KB threshold), then runs the check script once as root (it only reads the tree)

creates the system account nagios if absent (production's monitoring base provides it), then runs the check once as nagios through sudo -n (sudo logs it to the journal and /var/log/auth.log); the output goes to /run/p8test-fs-health/sudo.out

outcomes.outcome: the per-volume check script carries the base directory, the size threshold and the file count, and nagios may run it through sudo
an empty tree (at or under the size threshold) is reported CRITICAL with exit 2
a readable tree above the threshold is listed, a sample of its files read, and reported OK with exit 0, also when nagios runs it through sudo
a tree that cannot be listed, or a file whose content cannot be read, is reported CRITICAL

uncovered.why: the script runs as root (through sudo), which reads every file and directory; only an I/O error on the volume makes find or md5sum fail
uncovered.lifted_by: capability: fault injection on a lab volume (an I/O-error block device) inside a phase3 run
uncovered.evidence: the check runs as root via sudo (sysmon_fs_health.pp:10); phase3.py has no fault-injection step
